Aisha (Support): Heads-up - BetaBank (dedicated pool id: dp-betabank-03) opened a severity-2 about tail latency regressions after we flipped a quant profile last night. They report median ~320ms unchanged, but p95 jumped to ~900ms and p99 to ~1.6s. They can reliably trigger it with their standard batch workload. Ticket SB-9981.

Aisha (Support): Customer repro snippet they shared (using our SDK):
```
# node example
for (let i=0;i<200;i++) {
  await client.generate({model: 'gptx-13b', input: 'Explain sharding for DBs', maxTokens: 150});
}
```
They say p99 correlates with ~1-3 requests per minute where latency suddenly spikes.

Marco (eng-runtime): Which quant profile was rolled? And was fp8 enabled?

Aisha (Support): They noted profile "fp8_aggressive_v3" rolled on 2026-03-14T23:12Z and per-pool override int8=false, fp8=true.

Priya (eng-ml): fp8 aggressive + small calibration leads to outlier activations that trigger runtime checks and kernel fallback to fp16 path. Need to see rollout logs. The jitter you describe (1-3 req/min) smells like occasional range_violation checks or a periodic recompile.

sam-oncall: deploy-bot, show recent client rollouts and runtime fallback counters for dp-betabank-03.

deploy-bot: rollout: quant-profile fp8_aggressive_v3 -> dp-betabank-03 @2026-03-14T23:12:03Z
deploy-bot: fallback events: total=48 in 30m; reasons: range_violation=30, kernel_unavailable=18

Marco (eng-runtime): kernel_unavailable suggests the compiled int8/fp8 kernel requested by runtime wasn't present on some nodes -> runtime falls back to generic fp16 path with memcpy and slower kernel. If nodes are heterogeneous (driver versions, CUDA), we can see this.

Priya (eng-ml): Also check the quant manifest's bitwidth flag vs compiled artifact tags. Mis-tagging can cause runtime to ask for fp8 kernels not present. We recently changed artifact naming to include arch+driver, maybe the profile points at an artifact that isn't distributed to all nodes.

Aisha (Support): Customer confirms their pool has mixed node types: older A100s and newer H100s.

Marco (eng-runtime): Mixed HW + fp8 is risky. Immediate mitigations:
- Roll pool to model.variant=fp16 for the pool (fast, safe).
- Alternatively set runtime config: quant_profile.enforce_artifact_check=true to refuse to serve if kernel missing (prevents fallbacks but causes errors). Not ideal for customer.
- Schedule a staged redeploy of fp8 kernels to all nodes (longer).

Priya (eng-ml): Short-term, rebuild quant profile with per-layer emergency_scale and increase calibration sample size. For fp8 we should use N>=4000 for 13B to stabilize extremes; their manifest shows N=500. That's too low.

Aisha (Support): Customer asked for quick repro they can run to verify impact after change. Suggested script below to amplify tail events:
```
# warm + spike tester
for i in {1..30}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gptx-13b","input":"short","max_tokens":20}' >/dev/null; done
for i in {1..120}; do start=$(date +%s%3N); curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gptx-13b","input":"long explanation of distributed locks","max_tokens":300}' >/dev/null; echo "$(( $(date +%s%3N) - start ))"; sleep 0.5; done
```
This will show occasional spikes when fallbacks happen.

sam-oncall: I'm going to apply a runtime safety: pin dp-betabank-03 to fp16 variant and also add a temporary rule to route 100% of their traffic to fp16. Applying now.

deploy-bot: change queued: pool(dp-betabank-03).model.variant=fp16 by sam-oncall @2026-03-15T00:05:12Z
deploy-bot: change applied to 4 nodes.

Aisha (Support): I sent update to BetaBank. They ran their load and reported p99 dropped to ~680ms and p95 to ~380ms. They asked for root cause and a permanent path to use fp8 safely.

Priya (eng-ml): Proposed permanent plan:
1) Recreate quant profile with N>=4k representative sequences, include per-channel quantization and percentile clipping at 99.999th to limit outliers.
2) Ensure profile manifest includes required artifact tags for all cluster node types and verify artifact distribution step in CI.
3) Add validation stage: simulate small canary workload and compute synthetic fallback rate; fail rollout if fallback_rate>0.1%.
4) Update quant pipeline to reject N<1000 and require review for fp8 target.

Marco (eng-runtime): Platform changes:
- Emit realtime per-pool metric: kernel_fallback_rate and kernel_unavailable_count. Alert if fallback_rate > 0.2% within 10m during rollouts.
- Add a preflight check: compare profile.artifact_tags to node.inventory; block rollout if any node lacks artifact.
- Add a "safe-mode" for aggressive profiles that requires canary tag and min_calib_samples >= 2000.

sam-oncall: I'll file follow-ups: ENG-7012 (quant pipeline hardening) -> Priya, ENG-7013 (rollout preflight + metrics) -> Marco.

Aisha (Support): Noted. I'll close the support ticket after we confirm the follow-ups and BetaBank signs off on the rollback. They said thanks and will try canary runs once we publish the improved profile. :thumbsup:

Priya (eng-ml): One more note: fp8's dynamic range in attention layers can be sensitive; for certain prompt distributions per-token activation tails cause intermittent range checks. We should add a warning in the console when target profiles are fp8 and cluster contains mixed hardware.

Marco (eng-runtime): Agreed. Also we'll add a CLI tool for ops to quickly verify profile/node compatibility before rollout.

Aisha (Support): Closing the loop. Will re-open if BetaBank sees any re-regression.
